arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: General Verrilli argued the Federal Power Act expressly authorizes FERC to regulate wholesale rate processes.
Mr. Phillips argued economic principles support the Commission's approach to demand response.
Mr. Clement represented the Electric Power Supply Association and other power generator organizations.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission issued rules for wholesale demand response. These rules allow utilities to pay customers to reduce peak usage. The Electric Power Supply Association challenged these rules. They argued the rules intrude on state authority over retail rates.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between federal wholesale regulation and state retail control. It determines who sets the rules for peak electricity demand. The outcome shapes how utilities manage grid reliability and consumer costs.
